office: Washington Supreme Court, Justice Position 1 (unexpired 2-year term)
scope_plain: Every Washington voter. Nonpartisan: no party labels on the ballot. Washington uses a top-two system; because each of these races had exactly two candidates after filing, some skipped the August primary and appear only now. This is a 2-year unexpired term: Justice Mary Yu resigned Dec 31, 2025, Gov. Ferguson appointed Colleen Melody in January 2026, and the winner serves the rest of Yu's term, through 2028. Position 1 was on the August primary ballot because a third candidate (Laura Christensen Colberg) filed; Melody and Edwards advanced.
office_explainer: Highest state court. Nine justices have the final say on Washington law and the state constitution.
why_it_matters: The court decides whether state laws and initiatives square with the state constitution, including tax, school funding and civil rights cases. Justices normally serve six-year terms and must retire at the end of the year they turn 75. Five of the nine seats are on this ballot, more than usual, because two justices resigned and two chose not to run again.

candidates.name: Colleen Melody
candidates.background: Supreme Court justice since January 2026, appointed by Gov. Bob Ferguson to fill Justice Mary Yu's seat. Before that she led the Attorney General's Civil Rights Division and worked at the U.S. Department of Justice. UW undergraduate and law. Grew up in Spokane; lives in rural Western Washington.

own_words.text: "Now more than ever, state courts must safeguard our rights with independence and impartiality."
"Judges must anticipate and consider the law's impact on everyday people."
Pamphlet: as head of the AG's Civil Rights Division she "beat the Trump Administration" on the travel ban and family separation, and "returned millions in wages owed to workers."

candidates.name: Scott Edwards
candidates.background: Bainbridge Island tax and constitutional attorney; practice chair at Ballard Spahr/Lane Powell since 2010, previously at Perkins Coie. Adjunct professor at UW School of Law for more than 20 years. Princeton and UW Law. Has argued more than a dozen cases before the state Supreme Court.

own_words.text: "The role of the Supreme Court is to apply the constitution and laws as written, not rewrite them."
"Take politics out of the courtroom."
Wants "to bring an independent voice, principled judgment, and a focus on the rule of law."

candidates.name: David Stevens
candidates.background: Mason County Superior Court judge from Shelton. Navy veteran; former senior felony prosecutor, federal public defender, chief public defender for the Colville Confederated Tribes, federal prosecutor, and international prosecutor in Kosovo. UW and UW Law. Says he has tried more than 200 jury trials.

own_words.text: "Public policy is the province of the political branches and not the courts."
"I strongly favor judicial restraint and stare decisis."
Argues most justices now reach the court by governor's appointment rather than election, and that "Judge Stevens was elected and not appointed."

candidates.name: Jaime Michelle Hawk
candidates.background: King County Superior Court judge from Federal Way. Former federal public defender and ACLU of Washington attorney (the first ACLU-WA lawyer to become a judge), adjunct law professor, and member of the Supreme Court's Minority and Justice Commission. Gonzaga Law. First in her family to attend college.

own_words.text: "Courts should follow the law, protect people's rights, and treat everyone fairly."
"She has never had a trial overturned for legal error. She follows the law."
Pamphlet: Senators Murray and Cantwell appointed her to their federal judge selection committee; more than 100 current and retired judges endorse her.

candidates.name: Ian Birk

Before that, about 20 years in private practice representing individuals and small businesses in insurance, consumer protection and discrimination cases. UW and UW Law.

own_words.text: "Justice shouldn't depend on who you are or where you are."

candidates.name: Sean O'Donnell
candidates.background: King County Superior Court judge since 2013 (chief of the family law and criminal departments, mental health court lead judge) and Supreme Court justice pro tem. Before that, 12 years as a King County prosecutor, including the Green River Task Force. Georgetown and Seattle University Law.

own_words.text: "The values I bring to my job are compassion, fairness, independence, and honesty."
"The lack of legal aid for civil litigants will be the great challenge of the next decade."
Pamphlet: as chief family law judge "helped start a protection order court that resulted in hundreds of firearms being surrendered."

office: Washington Supreme Court, Justice Position 5 (unexpired 2-year term)
scope_plain: Every Washington voter. Nonpartisan: no party labels on the ballot. Washington uses a top-two system; because each of these races had exactly two candidates after filing, some skipped the August primary and appear only now. This is a 2-year unexpired term: Justice Barbara Madsen resigned April 3, 2026, Gov. Ferguson appointed Theo Angelis that month, and the winner serves the rest of Madsen's term, through 2028. Position 5 was on the August primary because a third candidate (Greg Miller) filed; Angelis and Larson advanced.
office_explainer: Highest state court. Nine justices have the final say on Washington law and the state constitution.
why_it_matters: The court decides whether state laws and initiatives square with the state constitution, including tax, school funding and civil rights cases. Justices normally serve six-year terms and must retire at the end of the year they turn 75. Five of the nine seats are on this ballot, more than usual, because two justices resigned and two chose not to run again.

candidates.name: Theo Angelis
candidates.background: Supreme Court justice since April 2026, appointed by Gov. Ferguson to fill Justice Barbara Madsen's seat. Previously a 26-year partner at K&L Gates in Seattle leading appellate and intellectual property teams, with pro bono work for immigrant children and veterans. Claremont McKenna, Oxford, LSE and Yale Law. First justice of Middle Eastern descent on the court.

own_words.text: "A fair, independent, and efficient judiciary is the bedrock of a healthy society."
"Precedent must never be overruled simply because the membership of the court has changed."
Pamphlet: "I sued the federal government when they forced children, as young as 4 years old, to appear without lawyers in immigration court."

candidates.name: Dave Larson
candidates.background: Retired Federal Way Municipal Court judge (18 years on the bench, 2008 to 2025) and 23 years as a trial lawyer; former mediator and arbitrator and Federal Way School Board president. Lives in Ellensburg. Seattle University Law and University of Puget Sound.

own_words.text: "We don't need to be tougher or softer on crime; we need to be smarter on crime."
"Our Supreme Court needs to be part of the solution and not part of the problem."
Pamphlet: says the court's decisions have "weakened" trial courts' response to crime and addiction, and he would "help fix current problems."

why_it_matters: The court decides whether state laws and initiatives square with the state constitution, including tax, school funding and civil rights cases. Justices normally serve six-year terms and must retire at the end of the year they turn 75. Five of the nine seats are on this ballot, more than usual, because two justices resigned and two chose not to run again.

candidates.name: Debra L. Stephens
candidates.background: Justice since 2008 and the court's current chief justice (chosen by the other justices). From Spokane; previously a Court of Appeals judge (2007) and an appellate attorney and Gonzaga law professor. Re-elected in 2014 and 2020. First woman from Eastern Washington on the court. Wrote the McCleary school-funding decision.

own_words.text: "I approach the law with judicial humility and a deep respect for text and structure."
"In an era of growing attempts to politicize the judiciary, I work every day to maintain the integrity and independence of our courts."
Pamphlet: cites "a proven record of expanding access to justice, improving efficiency and transparency."

candidates.name: Todd A. Bloom
candidates.background: Tacoma-area attorney (Todd A. Bloom, PLLC), CPA, CFA and CFP, with more than two decades advising companies and families and a decade as a tax attorney at major accounting firms. Navy officer on active duty 2002 to 2013 after being recalled post-9/11. Member of the WSBA Board of Governors. Tulane JD/MBA, UW LL.M. No campaign website listed in the pamphlet (contact: electtoddbloom@gmail.com).

own_words.text: "My judicial philosophy is rooted in the belief that judges must faithfully interpret and apply the law."
"This year's election is a choice: whether to retain the current justices or to give someone new your vote."
Pamphlet: says he represents "meaningful new perspective, experience, and common sense which will bring balance to the court."
